title: Plato: Complete Works
author: Plato (Edited by John M. Cooper, Associate Editor D.S. Hutchinson)
edition_analyzed: 1997 Hackett Publishing Company, edited by John M. Cooper
target_audience: Students and scholars of philosophy and classics
Readers interested in Western intellectual history
Anyone seeking a comprehensive primary source collection of Plato's works
core_themes: The nature of reality and knowledge (epistemology and metaphysics)
Ethics and the best way of life
primary_purpose: To present the full range of Plato's writings—including seminal dialogues, letters, and fragments—allowing readers direct engagement with foundational texts of Western philosophy and wisdom.

structure_format.narrative_style: Dialogue (Socratic method), occasionally mythic or allegorical; mostly conversational and dialectical
structure_format.organization: Chronologically and thematically arranged by editors; includes all known dialogues, letters, and spurious works plus notes and scholarly introductions
features: Extensive scholarly footnotes and explanatory introductions
Clarification of disputed and attributed works

key_concepts_lessons: The Socratic method as a way to elicit truth through questioning
Theory of Forms: the existence of perfect, immaterial models for all things
The tripartite nature of the soul—reason, spirit, and appetite
Philosopher-kings as rulers of the ideal state
Education as a means to cultivate virtue and wisdom
The immortality of the soul and the philosophical life as preparation for death
Critique of democracy, rhetoric, and sophistry
notable_features: Includes all surviving authentic dialogues (Apology, Republic, Symposium, Phaedrus, etc.), letters, and disputed works
Renowned translations by leading scholars, ensuring clarity and accuracy
Detailed editor's introductions and interpretive essays
Useful as a single-volume reference for academic and personal study
cultural_historical_context: Compiled in the late 20th century, using the best available manuscripts and scholarship, this edition makes Plato's works widely accessible in modern English. Plato’s writings, originally crafted in 4th century BCE Athens, laid the foundations of Western philosophy, political theory, and pedagogy. The Cooper edition remains the standard for students, scholars, and general readers.
reception_impact: Regarded as the definitive modern English edition of Plato's corpus
Standard text for academic courses on Plato and Ancient Philosophy
Praised for scholarly rigor, comprehensiveness, and readability
Fundamental for the study of philosophy, influencing countless thinkers and traditions
comparable_titles: The Complete Works of Aristotle (Edited by Jonathan Barnes)
The Presocratic Philosophers by G.S. Kirk, J.E. Raven, and M. Schofield
The Basic Works of Stoicism (Epictetus, Seneca, Marcus Aurelius)
